extracted.intended_audience: health insurers, Exchanges, QHP issuers, agents/brokers, state agencies, CMS-regulated entities, and legal/regulatory stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule preamble clarifying the scope and application of nondiscrimination protections under section 1557 and related CMS regulations, including that 'sex' discrimination encompasses sex characteristics, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, and sex stereotypes, and explaining who and how the rule applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'sex' discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalizes that the term 'sex' includes discrimination on the basis of sex characteristics, including intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision is finalized throughout multiple regulations (e.g., 42 CFR 438.3(d)(4), 438.206(c)(2), 440.262, 45 CFR 147.104(e), 155.120(c), 155.220(j), 156.125(b), 156.200(e), 156.1230(b)). The preamble explains this clarification will better ensure fair access to care, address disparities for LGBTQI+ individuals, and align policy across Exchange/QHP and section 1557 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: When regs require actions 'regardless of sex', include expanded characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Where regulations require actions to be taken 'regardless of sex', that requirement includes actions regardless of sex characteristics (including intersex traits), pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity, and sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied consistently to regulatory language that uses 'regardless of sex' to ensure nondiscriminatory treatment across the listed attributes; intended to prevent benefit designs or practices that have the effect of discriminating against persons with these characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PACE participant nondiscrimination protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Add sexual orientation and gender identity to the list of characteristics that may not serve as a basis for discrimination against a PACE participant (amendments to 42 CFR 460.98(b)(3) and 42 CFR 460.112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PACE provision is effective one year after the final rule's effective date. The preamble clarifies the change does not require PACE organizations to cover any particular item or service not already covered, but protects participants from discriminatory denial or barriers to services.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandate to cover particular procedures or treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule does not require entities to cover any particular procedure or treatment; amending nondiscrimination protections is not a mandate to include new coverages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if a covered entity provides coverage for a particular health service, it must provide that coverage to all individuals in a neutral, nondiscriminatory manner consistent with the rule. The preamble references Medicare practice (MACs/MA plans making local determinations) and notes medical necessity determinations remain relevant to whether denial is unlawful discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entities subject to the amended nondiscrimination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments apply to specified regulated entities: health insurance issuers offering non-grandfathered group or individual coverage (and their officials, employees, agents, representatives); States and Exchanges carrying out Exchange requirements; agents, brokers, or web-brokers assisting with enrollment through an FFE; QHPs in the individual and small-group markets; issuers providing EHB; and issuers using direct enrollment on an FFE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble specifies the relevant CFR sections (45 CFR 147.104(e); 155.120(c); 155.220(j); 156.125(b); 156.200(e); 156.1230(b)) and explains which market segments each amendment covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments do not apply to health care providers
rubrics_metrics.description: The nondiscrimination amendments finalized at the listed regulatory sections do not apply to health care providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explicitly responds to commenters and clarifies that applicability is limited to insurers, Exchanges, agents/brokers, and similar entities—not clinicians or provider organizations (unless otherwise covered by distinct provider-facing rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of provisions and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the specified provisions (or an application of a provision) is held invalid or unenforceable, that provision or application shall be considered severable from the remainder; a determination of invalidity or unenforceability does not affect the remainder of the section or other sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule contains a severability statement covering 45 CFR 147.104(e); 155.120(c); 155.220(j); 156.125(b); 156.200(e); and 156.1230(b), and explains that an invalidation as applied to particular persons/circumstances does not automatically invalidate application to other persons/circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom and conscience protections (RFRA) compliance and process
rubrics_metrics.description: In enforcing nondiscrimination provisions, the Department will comply with laws protecting the exercise of conscience and religion, including RFRA and other applicable legal requirements; no blanket religious exemption is created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entity alleging RFRA conflict should contact CMS for RFRA-based requests related to CMS-run programs or file a complaint with HHS OCR for religious freedom/conscience claims. The preamble describes the RFRA analysis (substantial burden → compelling interest and least restrictive means) and states the government's compelling interest is to improve health outcomes and fulfill the ACA's nondiscrimination command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender expression and transgender status encompassed by gender identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender expression and transgender status are considered inextricably linked to gender identity and are sufficiently addressed by inclusion of 'gender identity' in the nondiscrimination description of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification responds to public comments urging explicit inclusion of gender expression and transgender status to prevent evasion; the preamble explains that including 'gender identity' captures related forms of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and interpretive alignment (Bostock, Price Waterhouse, ACA/PHS Act authorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department relies on authority from ACA sections (e.g., 1311(c)(1)(A), 1312(e), 1321(a)) and PHS Act sections (2702 and 2792) to support the amendments and aligns the interpretation (that sex includes sexual orientation and gender identity) with Bostock and Price Waterhouse precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble rejects arguments that Title VII or Title IX frameworks are being misapplied, explains why Bostock supports the inclusion of sexual orientation and gender identity under sex discrimination, and cites statutory bases for regulating Exchanges, QHPs, and EHB-related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with Essential Health Benefits (EHB) and non-discriminatory benefit design
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 nondiscrimination requirements are separate from EHB nondiscriminatory benefit design requirements, but the rule finalizes language intended to ease compliance for entities subject to both and notes CMS will address EHB non-discriminatory benefit design in future rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble clarifies that §156.125(b) requires issuers providing EHB to comply with §156.200(e)'s nondiscrimination requirements and points readers to future CMS refinements on EHB nondiscriminatory benefit design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated costs and benefits: minimal administrative impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department anticipates minimal costs to regulated entities from clarifying sex discrimination because many entities already comply; any costs are justified by the benefits of protecting individuals from discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble references the Regulatory Impact Analysis and explains that prior prohibitions and prior compliance reduce expected burdens; CMS does not expect substantial administrative costs from describing sex discrimination more specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology change in 42 CFR 440.262: 'unique' to 'individualized'
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalizes the change of the term 'unique' to 'individualized' in 42 CFR 440.262 as proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble notes this technical revision alongside the nondiscrimination clarifications; intended to refine language regarding individualized participant care/plans.
